strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine gap between camera-controllable methods (single-image conditioning) and temporal methods (short clip conditioning)
Clear conceptual contribution: dual spatio-temporal conditioning with the insight that adjacency in video has both temporal and spatial components
Thoughtfully designed three-stage dynamic masking pipeline (optical flow → SAM2 → backward tracking) to separate static and dynamic elements
Practical engineering approach building on pretrained models with minimal modifications to preserve learned priors

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple dimensions (spatial consistency, camera control, video quality, geometric alignment) with strong quantitative improvements (77% MEt3R error reduction vs DFoT)
Good ablation studies validating key components (dynamic masking necessity, sensitivity to n)
Clear presentation with intuitive figures and methodology
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: individual components (dynamic SLAM, optical flow, SAM2, CoTracker) are existing work; main contribution is their combination rather than fundamental algorithmic innovation
Incomplete analysis of SLAM dependency: no systematic evaluation of robustness, failure modes, or degradation with poor reconstruction quality; computational costs not discussed

Limited evaluation diversity: quantitative results primarily on revisited viewpoints (can evaluate against input); no assessment of truly novel viewpoint prediction; evaluation limited to DynPose-100K and RealEstate10K

Weak baseline comparison: only direct comparison is DFoT; no comparison with other geometry-informed methods (Gen3C mentioned but not compared); camera-controllable baselines adapted ad-hoc, raising fairness concerns

Dynamic masking limitations: multiple thresholds and parameters (τ, etc.) with limited sensitivity analysis; cumulative failure modes of three-stage pipeline not discussed; backward tracking may miss objects moving only in later frames
Reproducibility gaps: dynamic masking hyperparameters not fully specified; SLAM configuration details missing; no mention of code release; training details unclear (augmentation, exact loss function)
Insufficient ablations: impact of different SLAM methods not explored; no analysis of alternatives to n=7 spatial frame selection; missing VAE encoder impact analysis
Real-world applicability claimed but not demonstrated (film production, VR mentioned as applications but not shown)
No perceptual evaluation: relies solely on automated metrics (FVD, VBench++) which may not fully capture scene consistency quality; missing user studies
Unclear generalization: performance on extremely static or highly dynamic scenes not analyzed; evaluation methodology compares to input frames assuming exact matching, which may not be necessary

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing clear limitations in existing camera-controllable video generation (short sequences, lack of long-term consistency)
Comprehensive multi-faceted evaluation across scene consistency (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS), geometric consistency (ME3R), video quality (FVD, VBench), and camera controllability metrics
Solid empirical results with substantial improvements over baseline (77% ME3R error reduction, significant LPIPS improvement in Table 1)

Thoughtful technical design: dual spatio-temporal conditioning elegantly combines temporal continuity with spatial consistency; dynamic masking pipeline effectively separates static and dynamic elements
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 4-8) systematically validating each design component and hyperparameter choices
Extends video generation capability to much longer sequences (100+ frames) with maintained consistency
Clear presentation with effective figures explaining the pipeline (Figures 3-5) and notation summary provided
Reproducibility commitment with promised code release and detailed implementation specifications
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: primarily integrates existing components (dynamic SLAM, SAM2, CoTracker3) rather than introducing fundamental innovation; dual conditioning mechanism is conceptually straightforward

Insufficient baseline comparisons: primary baseline (DFoT) is concurrent work from same authors; limited evaluation against other camera-controllable methods (CameraCtr1, MotionCtr1, AC3D); no comparison with other scene-consistent generation methods on equivalent metrics

Narrow experimental scope: evaluation limited to RealEstate10K (mostly static camera-only scenes) and DynPose-100K; no cross-dataset evaluation or testing on diverse real-world scenarios with extreme camera motion, heavy occlusions, or complex dynamics

Significant computational overhead: 4+ minutes inference time (Table 10) with majority spent in SLAM processing, making method impractical for interactive applications; optimized version still ~3 minutes

Technical fragility: success depends on cascading through multiple modules (SLAM, optical flow, SAM2, CoTracker3); no analysis of failure propagation; handling of challenging scenarios (occlusions, transparency, extreme depth) not addressed

Incomplete technical details: multiple heuristic thresholds in masking pipeline (e.g., L1 threshold in Eq. 6) not justified; sensitivity analysis missing; why specific geometric metrics (ME3R) chosen unclear; SLAM pose estimation accuracy impact not explored

Weak evaluation methodology: no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; single-run results without error estimates; fairness of comparison with concurrent baseline uncertain; limited failure case analysis

Generalization concerns: training on synthetic domains (RealEstate10K, OpenVid-1M); unclear how method generalizes to arbitrary diverse real-world videos; no robustness analysis across video types, lighting conditions, or aspect ratios

Limited scope of failure analysis: Appendix D superficially addresses limitations; marked failures in Figure 7 receive minimal discussion; no systematic analysis of failure modes or boundary conditions
Missing implementation details: loss functions not specified; training schedule and full hyperparameters incomplete; design choices lack explicit motivation (e.g., why n=7 for spatial adjacency)
